2024_197_8_c_rfp_2324_13_ahs_turf_bms_tr.page:
**Project and consultant**
Troy School District 2024 Synthetic Turf and Track Renovations, Athens High School and Baker Middle School, carried on the agenda as RFP 2324-13. Bids were due 1/29/24 at 11:00 A.M. The letter of recommendation is dated February 19, 2024 from Foresite Design, 3269 Coolidge Highway, Berkley, Michigan 48072, phone 248-547-7757, www.foresitedesign.com, signed by Michael Sims, and addressed to Rob Carson, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098. Copies went to Larry Franckowiak of Troy School District, Michelle Kerns/Mark Paulus of Lecole Planners, and the FDI file, with two enclosures. The project was separated into three trade categories, drawing a total of nine bids.

**Recommended awards**

| Category | Recommended firm | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Proposal A Site Work Turf | Nationwide Sports Construction, Valle Mines, Missouri | $635,250.00 |
| Proposal B Track Surface | A.G. Sports Services LLC, Jackson, Michigan | $122,200.00 |
| Proposal C Site Work Track | Nagle Paving Company, Novi, Michigan | $654,890.00 |
| Synthetic Turf (Sourcewell) | Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions, Inc. / Shaw Sports Turf, Calhoun, Georgia | $528,559.00 |
| **Total** | | **$1,940,899.00** |

Proposal A breaks down as a base bid of $519,250.00 plus Alternate No. 1 at $116,000.00. The alternate is a pre-manufactured performance pad matching the one installed at Troy HS in 2023, carrying a 24-year warranty and offering benefits for safety, athlete performance and maintenance. Proposal B is a base bid of $122,200.00 with no alternates; Proposal C is a base bid of $654,890.00.

**Bid tabulation (bids due 1/29/24 @ 11:00 A.M.)**

| Proposal | Bidder | Base bid | Alt 1 (Shock Pad) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A - Site Work Turf | Nationwide Sports Construction | $519,250.00 | $116,000.00 |
| A - Site Work Turf | S&H Trucking & Excavating | $581,000.00 | $70,000.00 |
| A - Site Work Turf | Gibraltar Construction Company | $736,000.00 | $130,000.00 |
| B - Track Surface | Current Surfaces | $113,334.00 | |
| B - Track Surface | AG Sports Services | $122,200.00 | |
| B - Track Surface | Star Trac Enterprise | $127,000.00 | |
| B - Track Surface | Goddard Coatings | $131,800.00 | |
| C - Site Work Track | Nagle Paving Company | $654,890.00 | |
| C - Site Work Track | Gibraltar Construction Co. | $898,000.00 | |

**Award exception**
The firm recommended for Proposal B was not the as-read low bidder; the as-read low bidder did not meet the Quality Assurance requirements of the specifications. Post-bid interviews with the apparent low bidders were conducted February 5th and 6th, and reference checks on both the apparent low bidder and the second low bidder returned good references.

**Sourcewell turf purchase**
Shaw Sports Turf's proposal is dated 20 December 2023 for the Athens High School Stadium Field in Troy, MI 48085: GameOn Hybrid 2.0 Synthetic Turf and Installation, 90,235 SF +/-, at $528,559, priced under Sourcewell Contract # 031622-SII through the Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Field Direct Purchasing Program. The district directed standardization of high school stadium turf systems on Shaw's GameOn system for Athens, and Foresite confirms the cost is in line with the 2023 installation. Shaw's territory manager is Jennifer Holton, phone 614.313.8772. The turf carries Shaw's standard eight-year manufacturer warranty on turf products, and the proposal expires 30 days after its date.
2024_197_8_c_rfp_2324_13_ahs_turf_bms_tr.verbose:
**Cover letter.** Foresite Design of 3269 Coolidge Highway, Berkley, Michigan 48072 (phone 248-547-7757, website www.foresitedesign.com) issued a letter of recommendation dated February 19, 2024 to Rob Carson, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098, regarding the Troy School District Athens High School & Baker Middle School 2024 Synthetic Turf and Track Renovations. The letter transmits a tabulation sheet of the bids submitted on January 29, 2024. The project was separated into three trade categories, for which a total of nine bids were received. The letter is signed by Michael Sims, notes two enclosures, and is copied to Larry Franckowiak of Troy School District, Michelle Kerns/Mark Paulus of Lecole Planners, and the FDI File. Foresite's practice areas are listed as Athletic Facility Planning, Site Planning, Consulting, and Landscape Architecture. The board agenda item title identifies the solicitation as RFP 2324-13, AHS Turf-BMS Track, Foresite, Bid Summary.

**Proposal A - Site Work Turf.** Foresite recommends Nationwide Sports Construction of Valle Mines, Missouri to complete the work identified in Proposal A Site Work Turf for a contract sum of $635,250.00. The breakdown is a Proposal A Base Bid of $519,250.00 plus Alternate No. 1 at $116,000.00, totaling $635,250.00. The recommended sum is based on acceptance of one base bid alternate covering installation of a pre-manufactured performance pad. That performance pad would match the one installed at Troy HS in 2023, includes a 24-year warranty, and would provide added benefits toward safety, athlete performance, and maintenance.

**Proposal B - Track Surface.** Foresite recommends A.G. Sports Services LLC of Jackson, Michigan for the work identified in Proposal B Track Surface for a contract sum of $122,200.00, consisting entirely of the Proposal B base bid of $122,200.00. The letter records that the vendor recommended for award was not the as-read low bidder for this category, because the as-read low bidder does not meet the Quality Assurance requirements of the specifications. Post-bid interviews with the apparent low bidders were conducted on February 5th and 6th, and post-bid interviews and reference checks were conducted with both the apparent low bidder and the second low bidder, each of which received good references.

**Proposal C - Site Work Track.** Foresite recommends Nagle Paving Company of Novi, Michigan for the work identified in Proposal C Site Work Track for a contract sum of $654,890.00, consisting of the Proposal C base bid of $654,890.00.

**Synthetic turf via Sourcewell cooperative purchasing.** Foresite recommends Shaw Sports Turf of Calhoun, Georgia for the Synthetic Turf work shown on the design drawings issued 12/4/23, for a contract sum of $528,559.00 under Sourcewell Contract # 031622-SII. The recommendation reflects the district's direction to standardize the high school stadium turf systems by incorporating Shaw's GameOn turf system for Athens, procured through the district's Sourcewell contract; Foresite Design reviewed the costs presented and confirms they are in line with what was installed in 2023.

**Total recommended for award.** Nationwide Sports Construction $635,250.00; A.G. Sports Services LLC $122,200.00; Nagle Paving Company $654,890.00; Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions, Inc. $528,559.00; total $1,940,899.00. Foresite asks to be advised of additional information required from the recommended contractors so it can be secured for presentation at the next Board of Education meeting.

**Bid tabulation sheets.** Three tabulation sheets are attached, each headed Troy School District 2024, Athnes High School Turf Track, Baker MS Track, Bids Due: 1/29/24 @ 11:00 A.M., dated 1/29/2024, with columns for bid security, Iran sanction disclosure, familial disclosure, addendum #1, base bid and remarks; bold indicates the apparent low bidder. Proposal A - Site Work Turf, where Alt 1 is the shock pad: Nationwide Sports Construction $519,250.00 base and $116,000.00 for Alternate 1; S&H Trucking & Excavating $581,000.00 base and $70,000.00 for Alternate 1; Gibraltar Construction Company $736,000.00 base and $130,000.00 for Alternate 1. Proposal B - Track Surface: Current Surfaces $113,334.00; AG Sports Services $122,200.00; Star Trac Enterprise $127,000.00; Goddard Coatings $131,800.00. Proposal C - Site Work Track: Nagle Paving Company $654,890.00; Gibraltar Construction Co. $898,000.00.

**Shaw Sports Turf proposal.** Dated 20 December 2023 and labeled Proposal 1, Synthetic Turf and Installation, for the project Athens High School - Stadium Field, Troy, MI 48085. Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions, Inc. (Shaw Sports Turf) quotes GameOn Hybrid 2.0 Synthetic Turf and Installation over an area of 90,235 SF +/- at $528,559. All appropriate taxes will be charged unless proof of tax-exempt status is supplied. Pricing is based on the Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Field Direct Purchasing Program, comprised of national and local cooperative and group purchasing organization contracts that provide predetermined and preferential pricing, and specifically on Sourcewell Contract # 031622-SII.

**Shaw scope inclusions.** Supply and install the Shaw Sports Turf system over base provided by others, including turf, sundries and infill materials, per manufacturer product specifications, warranty and installation methods; synthetic turf based on field sizing by Shaw Sports Turf, with layout changes possibly increasing price; standard Shaw Sports Turf colors, custom yarns not included; supply and install tufted and inlaid game field markings, comprising football and soccer lines and markings fully tufted into field panels, a Hawk logo at 2,100 SF maximum in three colors inlaid via traditional method, the letters ATHENS and RED HAWKS at height 24 feet in a quantity of 14 fully tufted into field panels, a D-Zone Agility Practice Area fully tufted, two 25 yard line A markings inlaid, and tick marks for men's and women's lacrosse inlaid; infill materials of ambient processed SBR and silica sand by weight; one GMAX test performed upon completion of each field; usable remnants of new material become property of the owner; standard Shaw adhesive; Shaw Sports Turf standard eight-year manufacturer warranty on turf products only; maintenance instruction and training plus review of the Shaw Sports Turf Maintenance manual; pricing based on the private wage schedule in effect at time of proposal and on one mobilization, with additional charges for further mobilizations.

**Shaw exclusions and conditions.** Excluded are bonds, bonding fees and additional insurance policies; prevailing, union wages or union requirements; design services, engineering, construction drawings, storm water management, architectural and engineering inspections, geotechnical testing, site survey and independent testing; contaminated, unsuitable or hazardous material removal and remediation including rock, disposal, analysis and testing; base work including aggregate provision or installation, compaction, grading and testing; independent testing of synthetic turf; storm water and sediment or erosion control measures beyond scope; additional detention or retention requirements; concrete pads or asphalt paving unless damaged during construction; field markings, lettering or logos not listed; civil site construction such as demolition, drainage systems, sub-grade work, soil stabilization, rock excavation, stone base, concrete curbs, nailer boards, asphalt paving, track surface and track and field events; utility work and irrigation removal or relocation; sports equipment, score clocks, bases, home plates, pitching rubbers, foul poles, soccer nets, corner flags, netting, goal posts and fence; maintenance beyond that listed; material storage fees or site security; any shock pad, E layer or drain tile unless included above; and protection for asphalt, concrete, landscaping and tracks unless identified. Conditions include force majeure relief with extension of the completion date, a staging area no more than 200 feet from the site, an executed contract approved by Shaw, payment terms set by Shaw Sports Turf Financial Services credit review, change orders for scope changes, no liquidated damages or penalty clauses, inspection of any reused infill, prices subject to increase for raw material, freight, manufacturing, labor and tax costs, prices subject to change after 30 days of the proposal date, and supply chain disruption affecting confirmation of the production date. The proposal expires 30 days after its date and is signed by Jennifer Holton, Territory Manager, Shaw Sports Turf, phone 614.313.8772.

2024_198_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.paragraph: The Michigan Association of School Boards 2024 Board of Directors election booklet sets out MASB's regional and pupil-membership group structure under Article IV of its bylaws, explains the email voting procedure for member boards, and prints statements and service records for fourteen candidates. Nine seats on the 24-member board are up for election, but only Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8 are contested and receive online ballots. Completed ballots had to be cast and confirmed by each district's superintendent secretary by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024.
2024_198_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.page:
**Membership structure (MASB Bylaws, Article IV, Section 2)**
Active members are the boards of education of Michigan public school districts, divided into eight regions along intermediate school district boundaries. Region 1 covers Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA and Menominee County ISD. Region 8 covers Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA, the region that includes Troy School District. Members are also divided into seven groups by pupil membership: Group I all intermediate districts; Group II 0-1,400; Group III 1,401-2,500; Group IV 2,501-5,000; Group V 5,001-11,000; Group VI 11,001-40,000; Group VII more than 40,000.

**Election rules**
The MASB Board of Directors has 24 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two per region, and one director each is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. The MASB President nominates the at-large director subject to board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 permits only one director from any one local or intermediate school district board. Article VIII, Section 8 provides that an unopposed nominee is declared elected without an election.

**Seats up in 2024**
Nine seats: Regions 1 (open seat), 2, 3 (one-year term), 4 (one-year term), 5, 6 (open seat), 7, 8, and Group V (one-year term). Region 1 is vacant because no nominations were received. Unopposed, with no ballots sent: Dawn Kaiser, Iosco RESA (Region 2); Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area Intermediate School District (Region 3); John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools (Region 4); Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools (Group V).

**Voting procedure**
Online balloting occurs in Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8. Each district received one ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Jan. 26, 2024, and it cannot be forwarded. Ballots must be cast and confirmed by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024. Unofficial results are posted on a voicemail recording at 517.327.5915, generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date, and emailed that afternoon; official results are approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors meeting. No local district or ISD funds may be used for campaigning, including district email accounts; questions go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929, or to Cheryl Huffman at 517.327.5915 or chuffman@masb.org.

**Candidates (incumbents noted)**

| Region | Candidate | District |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Janice Holz (incumbent) | Huron Intermediate School District, Huron County |
| 5 | Roshawnda Williams | Beecher Community School District, Genesee County |
| 6 | Robert Becker | Barry Intermediate School District, Barry County |
| 6 | Pamela Dickinson (incumbent) | Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County |
| 6 | Elizabeth O'Dell | St. Joseph County ISD, St. Joseph County |
| 6 | Andrew Robinson | Berrien RESA, Berrien County |
| 7 | Sharon Lee | Ypsilanti Community Schools, Washtenaw County |
| 7 | Michael McVey | Saline Area Schools, Washtenaw County |
| 7 | Jack Temsey | Eaton RESA, Eaton County |
| 7 | Mary Vincent | Monroe Public Schools, Monroe County |
| 7 | Dale Wingerd (incumbent) | Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee County |
| 8 | Melandie Hines | Wayne Westland Community Schools, Wayne County |
| 8 | Birgit McQuiston (incumbent) | Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County |
| 8 | Evelyn Pridemore | Redford Union School District, Wayne County |

All listed seats carry three-year terms. The booklet closes with MASB's mission statement: to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education, and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education for all students.
2024_198_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.verbose:
**Purpose and structure.** The 2024 MASB Board of Directors elections booklet opens with Article IV, Section 2 of the Michigan Association of School Boards bylaws, which provides that the board of education of any public school district in Michigan may become an active member, and that active members are divided into eight regions designated according to intermediate school district boundaries.

**Regions.** Region 1: Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA and Menominee County ISD. Region 2: Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona ESD, Charlevoix-Emmet ISD, Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle ESD, COOR ISD, Iosco RESA, Manistee ISD, Northwest Education Services and Wexford-Missaukee ISD. Region 3: Ionia County ISD, Kent ISD, Mecosta-Osceola ISD, Montcalm Area ISD, Muskegon Area ISD, Newaygo County RESA, Ottawa Area ISD and West Shore ESD. Region 4: Bay-Arenac ISD, Clare-Gladwin RESD, Clinton County RESA, Gratiot-Isabella RESD, Midland County ESA, Saginaw ISD and Shiawassee RESD. Region 5: Genesee ISD, Huron ISD, Lapeer County ISD, Sanilac ISD, St. Clair County RESA and Tuscola ISD. Region 6: Allegan Area ESA, Barry ISD, Berrien RESA, Branch ISD, Calhoun ISD, Heritage Southwest ISD, Kalamazoo RESA, St. Joseph County ISD and Van Buren ISD. Region 7: Eaton RESA, Hillsdale County ISD, Ingham ISD, Jackson County ISD, Lenawee ISD, Livingston ESA, Monroe County ISD and Washtenaw ISD. Region 8: Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA.

**Groups.** Active members are also divided into seven groups based on pupil membership: Group I, all intermediate districts; Group II, districts with 0 to 1,400 pupils; Group III, 1,401 to 2,500; Group IV, 2,501 to 5,000; Group V, 5,001 to 11,000; Group VI, 11,001 to 40,000; and Group VII, more than 40,000.

**Board composition and limitations.** Nine seats are up for election. The MASB Board of Directors is comprised of 24 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two elected from each region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. Directors are elected by active member school boards. The MASB President nominates a member to serve as an at-large director, subject to board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 of the MASB bylaws permits only one director to be elected or appointed from any one local or intermediate school district board. Article VIII, Section 8 provides that if any nomination is unopposed, the Board of Directors shall declare the unopposed candidate elected without conducting an election for that group or region.

**Seats and uncontested outcomes.** The seats up are Regions 1 (open seat), 2, 3 (one-year term), 4 (one-year term), 5, 6 (open seat), 7, 8 and Group V (one-year term), one seat each and three-year terms unless otherwise noted. Region 1 has a vacant seat as no nominations were received. Region 2 will continue to be represented by Dawn Kaiser, Iosco RESA, unopposed with no ballots sent. Region 3 will continue to be represented by Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area Intermediate School District, unopposed. Region 4 will continue to be represented by John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools, unopposed. Group V will continue to be represented by Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools, unopposed.

**Balloting.** Voting in Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8 takes place via online ballot. Each district received one ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Jan. 26, 2024; ballots cannot be forwarded. Completed ballots must be cast and confirmed by the superintendent secretary by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024. Unofficial results will be available on the voicemail recording at 517.327.5915, generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date, and emailed that afternoon. Official results will be approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors meeting, which newly elected directors should plan to attend. No local district or ISD funds may be used to campaign, which prohibits use of a school district email account; a personal email account must be used. Questions about expenditures of district funds go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., at bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929. An electronic file of physical and email addresses for the voting group or region is made available to each candidate under a revokable license limited to sharing information about the election. General questions go to Cheryl Huffman at 517.327.5915 or chuffman@masb.org.

**Region 5 candidates.** Janice Holz, incumbent, Huron Intermediate School District, Huron County: 32 years on this board and 25 years on the Bad Axe Public Schools board, holding President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer offices on both; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. She cites service as an ISD board member, current MASB Director and SET SEG Director, and names mental health, counselors, suicide prevention, social emotional support, artificial intelligence, student achievement, truancy, diversity, equity and inclusion, and administrator and teacher shortages as issues. Roshawnda Williams, Beecher Community School District, Genesee County: six years on the board as Treasurer, a resident of the Beecher School District for 15 years; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit and Award of Distinction; contact 810.936.1615 and roshawnda.williams63@gmail.com.

**Region 6 candidates.** Robert Becker, Barry Intermediate School District, Barry County: six years, offices President and Vice President, Certified Boardmember Award and Award of Merit; a former classroom teacher, central office administrator for operations and school superintendent who volunteers with Court Appointed Special Advocates, the Barry County Community Mental Health Authority, Barry ISD and the Family Support Center of Barry County, and has served on the MASB Government Relations Committee. Pamela Dickinson, incumbent, Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County: 10 years listed for time served, President for the last five years and a board member for nine years, offices President, Vice President and Treasurer; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty; currently a Member At-Large on the MASB Board of Directors. Elizabeth O'Dell, St. Joseph County ISD: 26 years on the board, offices President, Vice President and Treasurer; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award and the level 5 Master Diamond award; bachelor's degree from Ball State University and graduate degree from Western Michigan University; retired CEO of St. Joseph County Community Mental Health; volunteers with Red Cross Disaster Relief, substitute teaching and Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated. Andrew Robinson, Berrien RESA, Berrien County: three years, office Treasurer; nearing a Doctor of Education in Organizational Leadership and Development; works with Mosaic CCDA, a workforce and community development agency in Benton Harbor, and Emerge Innovation Hub, an entrepreneurial support organization in Southwest Michigan.

**Region 7 candidates.** Sharon Lee, Ypsilanti Community Schools, Washtenaw County: nine years, currently Vice President, offices President, Vice President and Secretary; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty; volunteers at Joyful Treats Community Development Corp., led by Ms. Khadija Wallace; cites A.L.I.C.E., Threat Assessment and Mental Health First Aid training and youth homelessness. Michael McVey, Saline Area Schools, Washtenaw County: seven years, offices President, Vice President and Secretary; over 40 years serving students and schools; former ELA and special education teacher who taught ESL for a year in Japan, authored "Meeting the Internet Challenge," trained teachers at The University of Arizona, earned a doctorate in Education, and is a professor of Teacher Education at Eastern Michigan University; past Washtenaw Association of School Boards president; will receive the President's Award this spring; serves on the Governmental Relations Committee. Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA, Eaton County: seven years on Eaton RESA and eight years on the Potterville Public Schools board, offices spanning President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer; MASB Curriculum and Instruction Committee, Government Relations Committee and its Vice Chairman, and former Vice Chairman of the Resolutions and Bylaws committee. Mary Vincent, Monroe Public Schools, Monroe County: two years, board Secretary entering her second year; bachelor's in K-12 music education and master's in K-12 administration and educational leadership; public school music teacher in southeast Michigan for 16 years teaching Y5 through 12; since May 2023 earned an Award of Merit, Data Specialty and Advocacy Specialty and serves on the MASB Resolutions and Bylaws Committee. Dale Wingerd, incumbent, Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee County: 17 years on this board and two years on the Lenawee ISD board, offices President and Secretary; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award and President's Award of Recognition; serving a second term with MASB.

**Region 8 candidates.** Melandie Hines, Wayne Westland Community Schools, Wayne County: 10 years, offices Vice President and Secretary; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction and Master Boardmember Award; states she helped pass a $150 million bond in 2018 across six communities named as Wayne, Westland, Dearborn Heights, Romulus and Inkster, and a $24.5 million bond for Westwood Community Schools, and is working on a skilled trades program with the Taylor Career Technical Center. Birgit McQuiston, incumbent, Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County: 12 years, offices President, Vice President and Secretary; certifications Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty; three years on the MASB Board of Directors serving on the Executive, Finance and Policy Committees, currently Chair of the Government Relations Committee, and appointed by the State Board of Education to a three-year term on the Special Education Advisory Committee; also serves on the Oakland County School Boards Association Board of Directors. Evelyn Pridemore, Redford Union School District, Wayne County: 11 years listed, almost 12 years of local service, offices President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer; currently President, recently appointed to the leadership team for WCASB; guided her district through deficit, declining enrollment, COVID, two superintendent searches and a multi-million-dollar bond initiative; married 36 years with three sons, two daughters-in-law and three grandchildren.

**Closing.** The booklet ends with the MASB mission statement: to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education, and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education for all students.

2024_199_2024_masb_bod_elections_booklet.verbose:
**Bylaws, Article IV, Membership, Section 2.** The board of education of any public school district in Michigan may become an active member of the association. Active members are divided into eight regions designated according to intermediate school district boundaries. Region 1: Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA and Menominee County ISD. Region 2: Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona ESD, Charlevoix-Emmet ISD, Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle ESD, COOR ISD, Iosco RESA, Manistee ISD, Northwest Education Services and Wexford-Missaukee ISD. Region 3: Ionia County ISD, Kent ISD, Mecosta-Osceola ISD, Montcalm Area ISD, Muskegon Area ISD, Newaygo County RESA, Ottawa Area ISD and West Shore ESD. Region 4: Bay-Arenac ISD, Clare-Gladwin RESD, Clinton County RESA, Gratiot-Isabella RESD, Midland County ESA, Saginaw ISD and Shiawassee RESD. Region 5: Genesee ISD, Huron ISD, Lapeer County ISD, Sanilac ISD, St. Clair County RESA and Tuscola ISD. Region 6: Allegan Area ESA, Barry ISD, Berrien RESA, Branch ISD, Calhoun ISD, Heritage Southwest ISD, Kalamazoo RESA, St. Joseph County ISD and Van Buren ISD. Region 7: Eaton RESA, Hillsdale County ISD, Ingham ISD, Jackson County ISD, Lenawee ISD, Livingston ESA, Monroe County ISD and Washtenaw ISD. Region 8: Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA. Active members are also divided into seven groups based on pupil membership: Group I, all intermediate districts; Group II, 0 to 1,400 pupils; Group III, 1,401 to 2,500; Group IV, 2,501 to 5,000; Group V, 5,001 to 11,000; Group VI, 11,001 to 40,000; Group VII, more than 40,000.

**Election framework.** Nine seats on the MASB Board of Directors are up for election. The board is comprised of 24 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two from each region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. Directors are elected by active member school boards, and the MASB President nominates a member to serve as an at-large director subject to board approval. Under Article VIII, Section 6, only one director may be elected or appointed from any one local or intermediate school district board. Under Article VIII, Section 8, an unopposed nomination results in the candidate being declared elected without an election for the uncontested group or region.

**Seats up and unopposed representatives.** Seats up for election, one each and three-year terms unless otherwise noted, are Regions 1 (open seat), 2, 3 (one-year term), 4 (one-year term), 5, 6 (open seat), 7, 8 and Group V (one-year term). Region 1 has a vacant seat because no nominations were received. Region 2 continues with Dawn Kaiser, Iosco RESA; Region 3 with Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area Intermediate School District; Region 4 with John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools; and Group V with Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools, all unopposed and with no ballots to be sent.

**Voting procedures.** Voting in Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8 takes place via online ballot. Each district received one ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Jan. 26, 2024, which cannot be forwarded. Completed ballots must be cast and confirmed by the superintendent secretary by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024. Unofficial election results will be available on the voicemail recording at 517.327.5915, generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date, and sent by email that afternoon; official results will be approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors meeting, which newly elected directors should plan to attend. No local district or ISD funds can be used to campaign for anyone running for a seat, a rule that prohibits candidates from using their school district email account to message other board members, so a personal email account must be used. Questions about what constitutes an expenditure of school district funds go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., at bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929. An electronic file containing physical and email addresses for the voting group or region is made available to each candidate under a revokable license limited to contacting school board members about the election. Other questions go to Cheryl Huffman at 517.327.5915 or chuffman@masb.org.

She serves as a current MASB Director and SET SEG Director and lists mental health, school counselors, suicide prevention, social emotional support, artificial intelligence, student achievement, truancy, diversity, equity and inclusion, and administrative and teacher shortages as priorities. Her contact information is 810.936.1615 and roshawnda.williams63@gmail.com.

**Region 6.** Robert Becker, Barry Intermediate School District, Barry County, six years, President and Vice President, Certified Boardmember Award and Award of Merit; a former classroom teacher, central office administrator for operations and school superintendent, he volunteers with Court Appointed Special Advocates, the Barry County Community Mental Health Authority, Barry Intermediate School District and the Family Support Center of Barry County, and has served on the MASB Government Relations Committee. Andrew Robinson, Berrien RESA, Berrien County, has served three years as Treasurer, is completing a Doctor of Education in Organizational Leadership and Development, and works with Mosaic CCDA, a workforce and community development agency in Benton Harbor, and Emerge Innovation Hub, an entrepreneurial support organization in Southwest Michigan.

**Region 7.** Sharon Lee, Ypsilanti Community Schools, Washtenaw County, nine years on the board and currently Vice President, with offices of President, Vice President and Secretary and certifications including the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty; she volunteers at Joyful Treats Community Development Corp., led by Ms. Khadija Wallace, and cites A.L.I.C.E., Threat Assessment and Mental Health First Aid training plus youth homelessness. Michael McVey, Saline Area Schools, Washtenaw County, seven years, offices of President, Vice President and Secretary, with the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition and Advocacy Specialty; he has spent over 40 years in education, taught ELA and special education, taught ESL for a year in Japan, authored "Meeting the Internet Challenge," trained teachers at The University of Arizona, earned a doctorate in Education, is a professor of Teacher Education at Eastern Michigan University, served as Washtenaw Association of School Boards president, will receive the President's Award this spring, and serves on the Governmental Relations Committee. Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA, Eaton County, seven years on Eaton RESA and eight years on the Potterville Public Schools board, currently serving again as President of Eaton RESA, has served on Policy, Community Relations, Technology, Building and Grounds, and Finance and Audit committees, and for MASB on the Curriculum and Instruction Committee and the Government Relations Committee including as its Vice Chairman, plus a concluded term as Vice Chairman of the Resolutions and Bylaws committee. Mary Vincent, Monroe Public Schools, Monroe County, two years and entering her second year as board secretary, holds a bachelor's degree in K-12 music education and a master's in K-12 administration and educational leadership, taught public school music in southeast Michigan for 16 years across grades Y5 to 12, and since May 2023 has earned an Award of Merit, Data Specialty and Advocacy Specialty while serving on the MASB Resolutions and Bylaws Committee. Dale Wingerd, incumbent, Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee County, lists 17 years on that board and two years on the Lenawee ISD board, offices of President and Secretary, and certifications including the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award and President's Award of Recognition; he has served two terms with MASB.

**Region 8.** Melandie Hines, Wayne Westland Community Schools, Wayne County, 10 years, Vice President and Secretary, with the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction and Master Boardmember Award; she states that in 2018 she helped pass a $150 million bond across six communities listed as Wayne, Westland, Dearborn Heights, Romulus and Inkster, recently helped pass a $24.5 million bond for Westwood Community Schools, and is working on a skilled trades program with the Taylor Career Technical Center. Birgit McQuiston, incumbent, Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County, 12 years, offices of President, Vice President and Secretary, with the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty; in three years on the MASB Board of Directors she has served on the Executive, Finance and Policy Committees, currently chairs the Government Relations Committee, and was appointed by the State Board of Education as the MASB representative to a three-year term on the Special Education Advisory Committee, which advises the State Board and the Michigan Department of Education. She also serves on the Oakland County School Boards Association Board of Directors. Evelyn Pridemore, Redford Union School District, Wayne County, 11 years listed and almost 12 years of service, offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer; she is currently President, was recently appointed to the leadership team for WCASB, has led her district through deficit, declining enrollment, COVID, two superintendent searches and a multi-million-dollar bond initiative, and has served on policy, finance, curriculum and facilities committees. She notes a husband of 36 years, three sons, two daughters-in-law and three grandchildren.

**Mission statement.** The booklet closes with the MASB mission: to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education, and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education for all students.

2024_200_soc_presentation.paragraph: Deputy Superintendent Rick West's Schools of Choice presentation and February 27, 2024 memo lay out the recommended non-resident enrollment program for the 2024-2025 school year, drawing on Plante Moran Cresa elementary enrollment projections, seventeen years of application history, and a demographic comparison of the district's 188 elementary Schools of Choice students with 4,897 non-Schools of Choice students. The recommendation is to accept Schools of Choice applications for 11 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 7 middle school students, the number identified through a sibling survey of current Schools of Choice families.

**Elementary enrollment projections submitted by Plante Moran Cresa.** The projection table compares the most likely projected counts with actual counts for kindergarten and first grade. **Schools of Choice students by building, 2023-2024.** A bar chart titled "Schools of Choice Students, Elementary Buildings, 2023-2024 School Year" is accompanied by a data summary comparing Schools of Choice and non-Schools of Choice students by building, giving the SOC count, the non-SOC count, the percentage of the building that is SOC, and the percentage change. **Projected Schools of Choice sibling preference placement.** A survey was emailed to current Schools of Choice families requesting information on siblings who would be eligible for kindergarten, first grade, and sixth, seventh and eighth grade for the 2024-2025 school year. The responses identify 11 kindergarten students planning to attend, 1 first grade student planning to attend, and 7 middle school students planning to attend across sixth, seventh and eighth grades combined, made up of 2 in sixth grade, 4 in seventh grade and 1 in eighth grade.

**Recommendation memo.** Dated Tuesday, February 27, 2024, from Rick West, Deputy Superintendent, to the TSD Board of Education, on the subject of Schools of Choice Recommendations for the 2024-2025 School Year. Factors considered were current enrollment across the Troy School District; enrollment projections, patterns and trends; the numbers and percentages of Schools of Choice students currently in the district; the projected number of Schools of Choice siblings who would be age-eligible to enter the district in 2024-2025 if a limited number of kindergarten, first and sixth through eighth grade students were admitted under Schools of Choice; and available elementary classrooms. The recommendations are to use the Plante Moran Cresa enrollment projection numbers as the foundation for determining the number of Schools of Choice students to admit for the coming school year; to accept Schools of Choice applications for 11 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 7 middle school students; and to place middle school students in a building according to available space. The memo notes that based on kindergarten applications received for 2024-2025, the district anticipates attracting many more than 11 applicants, which would allow the district to admit 11 kindergarteners initially with the option of admitting additional students, if space allows, in the third week of August.
